method: Manual comparison of each proposed article's engineering decision, argument sequence, and worked example against the nearest repository article. A distinct slug or low shingle score is not treated as originality.

http-425-early-data-replay-review.decisionComparison: The prior article authenticates and deduplicates repeated webhook events; this article decides whether an HTTP request exposed to TLS early-data replay must be deferred or retried with 425 across intermediary hops.
http-425-early-data-replay-review.workedExampleComparison: A synthetic reservation traverses a gateway twice with Early-Data: 1 and is retried after handshake completion, rather than replaying a signed webhook fixture.

http-etag-lost-update-review.decisionComparison: The prior article centers on user conflict recovery; this article defines strong validators, If-Match semantics, intermediary behavior, and an atomic persistence predicate.
http-etag-lost-update-review.workedExampleComparison: Ana and Ben's version-14 request demonstrates the wire and commit contract rather than only the conflict UI.

postgres-transaction-isolation-anomaly-h.decisionComparison: The prior work asks which failures can be retried; this article chooses isolation or constraint controls for a multi-row invariant.
postgres-transaction-isolation-anomaly-h.workedExampleComparison: Two barrier-synchronized sessions produce write skew, rather than replaying a serialization failure.

permissions-policy-iframe-delegation-rev.decisionComparison: The prior article stages resource restrictions through Content Security Policy; this article decides capability eligibility for exact document origins through Permissions-Policy inheritance and iframe container policy.
permissions-policy-iframe-delegation-rev.workedExampleComparison: An approved booking frame, unapproved sibling, and host page request synthetic geolocation under separate header and allow restrictions rather than loading a checkout resource from an undocumented host.

trusted-types-enforcement-rollout.decisionComparison: The prior article governs CSP deployment broadly; this one inventories DOM sinks and governs Trusted Type policy transformations before require-trusted-types-for enforcement.
trusted-types-enforcement-rollout.workedExampleComparison: The support-preview adversarial markup fixture exercises the policy-to-sink transformation boundary.

accessible-virtualized-list-test-handoff.decisionComparison: The prior work is a general accessibility regression lane; this article resolves logical identity, set position, recycled DOM, and focus behavior in a virtualized collection.
accessible-virtualized-list-test-handoff.workedExampleComparison: Keyboard movement from logical item 18 to 23 crosses and re-enters the mounted window.

terraform-moved-block-refactor-review.decisionComparison: The prior work reconciles unexplained remote drift; this article preserves state identity during an intentional address refactor.
terraform-moved-block-refactor-review.workedExampleComparison: A synthetic root resource moves into a child module while retaining the same remote ID.

kubernetes-server-side-apply-ownership-r.decisionComparison: The prior work decides readiness; this article resolves field-manager ownership and whether a conflict may be forced.
kubernetes-server-side-apply-ownership-r.workedExampleComparison: An autoscaler and release manager contend specifically over Deployment replicas.

email-dmarc-alignment-delegated-sender-r.decisionComparison: The prior work governs bounce-state handling; this article proves SPF or DKIM organizational-domain alignment for a delegated sender.
email-dmarc-alignment-delegated-sender-r.workedExampleComparison: Receiver headers show SPF passing for a vendor bounce domain while visible-From alignment still fails.

postgres-exclusion-constraint-booking-re.decisionComparison: The prior study classifies transaction failures for retry; this article moves a room-and-time non-overlap invariant into a GiST exclusion constraint with explicit range semantics.
postgres-exclusion-constraint-booking-re.workedExampleComparison: Two barrier-synchronized sessions attempt overlapping Cedar reservations plus adjacent and cross-room controls, rather than replaying a failed transaction to decide retry safety.

css-container-query-component-test-hando.decisionComparison: The prior work selects viewport cohorts for a journey; this article derives a component breakpoint from containing-block failure independent of viewport.
css-container-query-component-test-hando.workedExampleComparison: One pricing card is measured around its failure width while embedded in three different hosts.

http-message-signature-proxy-boundary-re.decisionComparison: The prior work delegates bearer authority; this article fixes covered HTTP component canonicalization across proxy rewrites.
http-message-signature-proxy-boundary-re.workedExampleComparison: Host and path mutations around a signed command reveal which representation each hop verifies.

offshore-developer-nodejs-worker-transfe.decisionComparison: The prior study measures AsyncLocalStorage propagation and request-context contamination; this study decides between structured cloning, ArrayBuffer transfer, and shared memory for worker-thread buffer ownership, including detachment, cancellation, worker failure, and replacement.
offshore-developer-nodejs-worker-transfe.workedExampleComparison: Aliased TypedArray and DataView slices plus pooled Buffer views cross clone, transfer, and shared-memory cases; the fixture does not reuse the prior study's interleaved request markers.

offshore-developer-postgresql-listen-not.decisionComparison: The prior study asks what atomic outbox persistence guarantees across a downstream relay and consumer effect; this study decides whether PostgreSQL LISTEN/NOTIFY may reduce wake latency while a queryable cursor remains the sole recovery path, with PostgreSQL-specific startup, transaction, duplicate-folding, and queue rules.
offshore-developer-postgresql-listen-not.workedExampleComparison: A listener is cut in four windows around LISTEN commit, wake receipt, outbox query, and checkpoint commit, then must recover by cursor; the prior study follows one transaction through a generic relay and downstream message duplicate.

offshore-developer-playwright-auth-state.decisionComparison: The prior study decides whether trace artifacts are safe to share; this one prevents account and tenant state leakage between parallel BrowserContexts.
offshore-developer-playwright-auth-state.workedExampleComparison: Member-A and member-B workers use cross-tenant tripwires under parallel execution.

offshore-developer-kubernetes-statefulse.decisionComparison: The prior study decides eviction feasibility during a node drain under disruption budgets; this study decides how rollingUpdate.partition stages StatefulSet template revisions while preserving ordinal, claim, readiness, and rollback evidence.
offshore-developer-kubernetes-statefulse.workedExampleComparison: A three-ordinal StatefulSet updates ledger-2 then ledger-1, stops on a seeded readiness failure, checks persistent markers, and rehearses mixed-revision rollback; it does not evict Pods or vary a disruption budget.

offshore-developer-nextjs-server-action-.decisionComparison: Both treat Server Actions as directly reachable endpoints and test identity, object authorization, origin/proxy handling, denied cases, and side effects.
offshore-developer-nextjs-server-action-.workedExampleComparison: Member-B replaying a captured action against member-A's object repeats the prior cross-tenant direct-request fixture.
